## Delivery Budget

- Estimate confidence: medium

| ID | Work item | Effort | Architecture delta | Debt claim | Addresses | Rationale |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| W1 | Schema grammar and governing projection | 5 | 1 | - | - | New pure module with marker failures, fence opacity, note splices, and checkbox reuse. Effort 5 is the new abstraction. Architecture +1 is the permanent reader every later phase calls. Tests for the grammar belong to this item. |
| W2 | Authority wiring and schema fields on bindings | 5 | 1 | - | - | Drift, parsers, spans, baselines, admission, and completion must share one expected-schema input. Effort 5 crosses those subsystems. Architecture +1 keeps schema 0 and schema 1 as concurrent record contracts without a version bump. |
| W3 | Recorded schema migration and recovery commands | 8 | 2 | - | - | Adds a lineage kind, digest-bound operator and reviewer authority, and idempotent registration for both unbound approvals and drift-blocked runs. Effort 8 is that migration. Architecture +2 is the lasting record kind and the two authority modes on top of the existing store. |
| W4 | Schema 1 workflow assets and rendered instruction | 5 | 1 | - | - | Publishes the skeleton, skills, templates, diagnostics, and override behavior across harness install and both delegation modes. Effort 5 matches that asset surface, including the required upgrade and skill acceptance suite. Architecture +1 is the new supported migration skill. |

Tests belong to the work item they validate. No negative architecture delta is claimed. Schema 0 support is retained on purpose, so this feature does not simplify away an existing path.

### Surface Snapshot

- Subsystems: 4
- Production files: 42
- Persistent/external boundaries: 2
- New shared abstractions or public contracts: 1
- New persistent schemas: 1

Subsystems are the plan-document projection, review governance and records, the migration commands, and shipped workflow assets. The production-file count is the Files Touched table. The two boundaries are the existing RecordStore streams and Git commit blobs. There is no new external service. The new abstraction is `loadPlanDocument`. The new persistent schema is the `plan-schema-migration` budget payload. Optional binding fields extend the version-1 payload and are not a second schema and not a SQLite migration. Phase 0 reconciles the file count if a cited module has moved. A new lock, a new stream, or a binding version bump requires this plan to be revised before that work is coded.

findings.title: Schema 1 text-amendment guard verification fails after any informational edit
findings.failure: On a schema 1 run, once a status line or note is edited, no text_only plan amendment can be verified and guarded author steps are blocked, so execution stalls.
findings.lowestCostCorrection: Choose and specify a schema-1 guard verification rule (projection-based fixed-segment check or accepting raw diffs only on non-governing lines), apply it to the unchanged check, and add status/note-then-amendment fixtures.

findings.title: authorityMarkdown blanking contradicts offset preservation
findings.failure: Plan-impact spans and protected ranges resolve to wrong raw byte offsets, authorizing or rejecting the wrong bytes.
findings.lowestCostCorrection: Specify blanking as replacing each non-newline UTF-16 code unit with a space (keeping CR/LF) and converting char ranges to bytes via the raw string; add a non-ASCII fixture.

findings.title: recover-plan earlier-phase section equality remains raw on schema 1
findings.failure: A permitted note in an earlier phase blocks all later frontier recoveries with an Earlier phase changed rejection.
findings.lowestCostCorrection: Compare each earlier phase section by its governing comparison projection on schema 1, list the site in section 2.2, and add a fixture.

findings.title: Reviewer-authority migration path is unreachable and unspecified
findings.failure: The reviewer authority mode advertised by the plan and skill can never succeed, leaving dead code and misleading operator guidance.
findings.lowestCostCorrection: Decide whether to define a focused reviewer approval mechanism (run, prompt context, route) or ship operator-only confirmation for this feature and update section 3.3, tests and skill.

findings.title: migrate-schema must refuse when expected schema is already 1
findings.failure: A repeated or schema-1-binding migration irreversibly drift-blocks the run with an invalid lineage.
findings.lowestCostCorrection: Refuse with PLAN_MIGRATION_CONFLICT before dry-run/write when the binding has planSchema 1, lineage already holds a valid migration, or the source run has a migration record; add tests.

findings.title: Exclusion diff alignment and currentText pairing are undefined
findings.failure: Dry-run and record can compute different exclusions/digests, or the motivating dry-run cannot show the current status text as required.
findings.lowestCostCorrection: Name a deterministic line diff with stable tie-breaking and record one hashed nonGoverningText block of target non-governing lines instead of per-exclusion pairing.

findings.title: expectedKeys omits the decisions stream that recover-plan includes
findings.failure: A concurrent review decision does not invalidate a migration attempt, unlike recover-plan.
findings.lowestCostCorrection: Include the decisions key list in expectedKeys in Design Decisions and section 3.3.

baselineAssessment.reason: Projection module (~5), schema threading across ~30 drift/parser/span call sites plus bind (~6), dual-entry migration with digest, atomic append, bind integration and refusal rules (~8), assets/templates/skills/acceptance (~5), plus schema-1 text-amendment verification the plan omits (~2-3).
